name: Storage and cookie availability flags
plain: Tests whether cookies, localStorage, sessionStorage and IndexedDB work.
meaning: Four booleans plus openDatabase and addBehavior legacy checks. Almost always all true, so low entropy, but they flag locked-down privacy modes and blocked storage.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

story.what_it_is: Checks whether cookies and browser storage work, which shows locked down privacy settings.
story.for_you: You never see it. A site quickly tests whether it can save a small note in your browser. If it cannot, you may see a message like Please enable cookies, or a feature may stop working.
story.for_makers: Sites need storage for logins, carts and settings. They check first so the page does not break. The answers also reveal locked down privacy settings, so fraud teams use them too.

use_cases.example: A shop tests whether cookies work, and if not, shows a warning that your cart will not be saved.
A browser game checks if it can save progress, and warns that scores will not be kept when storage is blocked.
A bank login shows a clear Please enable cookies message instead of a blank error.
A bot defence tool notes visitors with all storage blocked as slightly more risky.
An analytics tag falls back to server side counting when it cannot save a cookie.
An online course asks students to enable storage so lesson progress is saved.
An ad vendor skips cookie based targeting if storage is blocked.

linkedin.how: Storage features detected (BleepingComputer). Read by the LinkedIn APFC fingerprint script (48 features, alleged by BrowserGate, partly confirmed by BleepingComputer).
